parsed.explanation: Combined operative regime: no documented border, facility, custody or care rule that targets trans visitors, and same-sex conduct is not criminalised. The main documented exposure is state-linked policing of LGBTQ spaces: a single located raid on a venue in one city, with about 30 detained, warrantless entry, extortion, and a charge with no basis in national law. Reporting describes intensified persecution after a disputed 2024 election, but it is not trans-specific and is undated in detail. No hate-crime or anti-discrimination statute covers gender identity, so recourse is thin. Documented positives are a 2016 supreme court ruling on family protection and a majority public opinion favouring equal rights. These are resident-facing or general signals and offset little. Thin trans-specific traveller data, so the rating rests on structural signals and the documented raid and persecution.

entry_documents.exposure: No documented border or entry rule targeting trans visitors. Visitors' home-issued documents are not shown to be examined or refused.
entry_documents.interaction: The dossier notes residents cannot obtain matching documents; this is resident-facing and not treated as visitor exposure.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: May 2026 police raid on an LGBTQ+ venue: about 30 detained, warrantless entry, extortion, and a false 'homosexuality' charge. Detention and extortion of queer people is documented, though only one located incident.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Local NGOs publicly denounced the raid; no documented prosecution of officers.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Police target venue patrons rather than visible trans individuals. A visiting trans person in such a venue would be exposed to the same pattern.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: No documented facility-access or custody-placement rule by birth sex. No documented national or subnational facility restriction.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: The subnational dossier records no regional variation; the single documented raid is in one city. Absence is not treated as a protection.

care_services.exposure: No general healthcare or transition-care provisions in law. Visitor-facing care denial is not documented.
care_services.interaction: Lack of statutory care means a visitor cannot rely on local care provision, and access in an emergency is not documented.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Police treat queer venues as targets and charge detainees with a non-existent offence. Post-2024 reporting describes persecution of LGBTQ people tied to the political crisis; the 2015 persecution of an openly gay parliamentarian is dated.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Supreme court actions occurred (2016 family ruling); the 2016 suspension of the 17 May resolution shows institutional reversal.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: State-linked persecution in a political crisis raises exposure for any visibly queer or trans person in affected venues.

minors_guardians.exposure: Same-sex couples cannot adopt; the 2016 ruling protects children of same-sex families. No documented rule affecting a visiting minor or guardian.
minors_guardians.protection: The 2016 supreme court ruling requires state protection of all families and grants children equal rights.
minors_guardians.interaction: Family-status rules are resident-facing; no traveller-specific minor exposure is documented.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No trans-specific violence rate documented. Absence of a hate-crime statute means no aggravated penalty for violence against trans people.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Public opinion majority favours equal rights (2023); no hate-crime or anti-discrimination statute covers gender identity.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Police response to violence is not documented; the venue raid suggests police are not reliable protectors for queer people.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No working legal gender recognition; the 2017 action is unresolved; the 2016 identity-card announcement has no procedure; the equal-marriage bill's fate is unrecorded.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Courts have ruled for family protection (2016); the 2016 ruling is documented as in force.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: A visitor who is detained or extorted has no recorded trans-specific remedy. Remedies for the raid are not documented.

anchor_checks.comparison: 0.35-A has a universal registry-based entry ban and routine exclusion of trans visitors. This dossier documents no border exclusion or registry, so it sits higher. It has a documented police-raid pattern, which keeps it below the 0.55 tier.

0.55-B has routine secondary screening and denial of entry for divergent records, with slow remedies. This dossier documents no comparable border screening, but it has a state raid with extortion and no recourse, so it is roughly similar or slightly lower.

0.75-C has respectful border treatment, a functioning tribunal and compensation for unlawful holding. This dossier lacks any operating trans-specific remedy and documents state extortion, so it sits clearly below.

parsed.synthesis: No documented trans-specific border, facility, custody or care exclusion applies to visitors. The operative exposure is a documented police raid on a queer venue with extortion and a baseless charge, plus post-election persecution reporting. Recourse is thin: no hate-crime or anti-discrimination statute covers gender identity and the raid has no recorded prosecution. Protective signals are real but mostly general or resident-facing: a 2016 family-protection ruling and a 2023 public majority favouring equal rights. The rating reflects a documented state-tolerated targeting pattern with thin recourse, and the thin trans-specific record means it is not lower.
